- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥1.0) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 2–5% for 30-day horizon.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75.0), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak or use 10-day moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment is negative (0.0) in last 3–5 days, model underestimates; add 1–3% to forecast mean, especially if recent price is below 70.0.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast is >75.0 and true outcome drops below 72.0, adjust downward by 1–2% for next 7-day horizon.
- Sentiment reversal (from 1.0 to 0.0) triggers downward bias; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5 days unless confirmed by new data.
- For 30d forecasts, if true outcome is consistently below 70.0 after 10+ days of high sentiment, model overconfidently holds high; apply downward correction of 2–4% for next 7 days.
